name: snarl-sopi-backend
description: Snarl and Sopi operator backend v6.75.0: backend theme step 2 — borders removed, bands instead of boxes, headings carry the structure, and the palette put to work. Referenced against moma.org screenshots. The reference separates almost nothing with a line: event rows, price rows and whole sections sit on whitespace, and a boundary is a change of background, not a border. The dashboard drew 163 borders from --line; black made them cages and grey would still have left 163 lines, so --line and --clay go transparent and --cream-shadow becomes a light grey field with white panels. Structure moves into type, which is where the reference keeps it: the page title was 21px italic, now 34px at weight 900, panel titles 700, totals 900, per the design system's own Display 900 / Heading 700. All 20 italic rules inherited from the Cormorant display face are straightened, listed explicitly so a genuine em still works. Shadows removed except focus rings. The revenue tile was pure black filled with bronze hexes hardcoded inside the renderer, so it could not be themed at all; those are now tokens in index.html holding their old values, and the theme points them at the palette — the tile becomes c-night, the one palette colour designed to take white text, with the week in sky and today in the yellow accent. Attention gets c-orange rather than sharing magenta with alerts. features.html now loads the same stylesheet, so the public page and the product behind it are visibly one thing. Verified in a browser: Libre Franklin applied, every sampled element square, no page errors, no failed assets, no horizontal scroll, and the public page still renders its images and language toggle. Cumulative over v6.74.0.
